q: What are the most common carbon accounting mistakes Indian SMEs make?
title: Common carbon accounting mistakes
short: The most common mistakes are using kVAh as kWh, counting the same bill twice, putting GST-inclusive amounts into spend-based factors, mixing up billing date and consumption period, putting diesel generators and rented space in the wrong scope, and using a grid factor without naming its source and edition.

ul: Treating kVAh on an HT bill as kWh. kVAh is higher whenever the power factor is below 1, so it overstates Scope 2.
Counting units exported under net metering as consumption, or subtracting solar you generated from units you bought twice.
Assigning a bill to the month it was issued, not the period it covers, which breaks month to month comparison and year-end cut-off.
Using a combined margin or an old grid factor instead of the CEA weighted average for the edition you report against.
Putting diesel for a generator in Scope 2 because it makes electricity. Fuel you burn is Scope 1.
Counting fuel bought in the year as fuel burnt, without allowing for a large stock change in the tank or yard.
Converting LPG in litres when the invoice is in kg, or PNG in kg when it is in scm. Match the factor's unit to the invoice.
Leaving out small sources such as forklifts, canteen LPG or company cars, without saying they were excluded.
The same invoice uploaded twice, once as a scan and once as an email PDF, both counted.
Spend-based Scope 3 on amounts that include GST, which inflates the figure by the tax rate.
No record of which factor, source and edition were used, so the figure cannot be checked next year.
Mixing CO2 and CO2e totals without saying which gases are included.

sections.h: A quick self-check before you send figures
ol: Do monthly kWh and fuel quantities trace to a bill for every month and every meter?
Is every factor written with its source, edition and unit?
Is each source in one scope only, and listed exclusions stated?
Does the total move by month in line with production, or is there an unexplained spike?

example.title: Illustrative: how three mistakes add up for one factory
lines: kVAh used as kWh: 1,00,000 kVAh at power factor 0.95 is 95,000 kWh; overstated by 5,000 kWh x 0.710 = 3,550 kg CO2
One month's bill counted twice: 42,000 kWh x 0.710 = 29,820 kg CO2 added
Generator diesel moved from Scope 2 to Scope 1: the total stays the same, but the scope split changes
Errors in the total: 3,550 + 29,820 = 33,370 kg, about 33.4 tonnes CO2 too high
